issue.title: Add a jsonl-lint tool that reports every invalid JSONL row with its line number
issue.problem: The repository has no tools at all yet: there is no packages/ directory, the README says 'No tools yet: packages/ is empty', and the root `npm test` just prints 'no workspaces under packages/'. There is nothing in the repo that can check a JSONL journal, so a torn or hand-edited row is only found when a reader breaks on it.
issue.reason: Journals are kept as JSONL, and one torn or hand-edited row breaks the readers. A linter that names every bad row by line number, and fails with a non-zero exit, lets a person or a script find and fix the damage before a reader hits it.
issue.outcome: A new npm workspace under packages/ provides a `jsonl-lint` command: given a file, it reports every row that is not valid JSON with its 1-based line number and exits non-zero if there are any; it exits 0 on a clean file; and a missing file is reported as an error with a non-zero exit. The tool has a node:test suite that the root `npm test` runs, and the README lists it.
expect: After `npm ci` at the repo root, `npx --no-install jsonl-lint <file>` runs the tool (the workspace package declares a `jsonl-lint` bin), and `npm ci` succeeds with the committed package-lock.json.

On a file whose every row is valid JSON (e.g. `{"a":1}
[1,2]
"x"
42
` with a trailing newline), `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 0 and prints no row report.

On a file with rows 1 `{"a":1}`, 2 `{"a":`, 3 `{"b":2}`, 4 `not json`, 5 `{"c":3}`, `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 1 and its output (stdout plus stderr) contains exactly two row reports: one line starting `<file>:2:` and one line starting `<file>:4:`, and no line starting `<file>:1:`, `<file>:3:` or `<file>:5:`.
A last row with no trailing newline is still checked: on a file `{"a":1}\n{"a":` (no final newline), `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 1 and reports a line starting `<file>:2:`.
Rows ending in CRLF are judged on their content: on a file `{"a":1}\r\n{"b":2}\r\n`, `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 0.

On a path that does not exist, `jsonl-lint /nonexistent/journal.jsonl` exits 2, writes a message to stderr that contains the path `/nonexistent/journal.jsonl`, and prints no JavaScript stack trace (no line beginning with whitespace then `at `).
Run with no file argument, `jsonl-lint` exits 2 and writes a usage message to stderr.

The new workspace has a `test` script running `node:test` tests that cover a clean file, a file with invalid rows (checking the reported line numbers and exit code 1) and a missing file (exit code 2); the root `npm test` runs them and passes.
The package has no runtime `dependencies` in its package.json and is plain ES modules with no build step.
README.md's 'What is here' section no longer says there are no tools and lists jsonl-lint with how to run it.

proofs.line: After `npm ci` at the repo root, `npx --no-install jsonl-lint <file>` runs the tool (the workspace package declares a `jsonl-lint` bin), and `npm ci` succeeds with the committed package-lock.json.
proofs.how: At the PR head: `npm ci && printf '{"a":1}\n' > /tmp/ok.jsonl && npx --no-install jsonl-lint /tmp/ok.jsonl; echo exit=$?` — npm ci succeeds and the command runs (exit=0). Also `grep -r '"jsonl-lint"' packages/*/package.json` shows the bin entry.

proofs.line:
On a file whose every row is valid JSON (e.g. `{"a":1}
[1,2]
"x"
42
` with a trailing newline), `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 0 and prints no row report.
proofs.how:
`printf '{"a":1}
[1,2]
"x"
42
' > /tmp/clean.jsonl; npx --no-install jsonl-lint /tmp/clean.jsonl > /tmp/out 2>&1; echo exit=$?; grep -c '^/tmp/clean.jsonl:' /tmp/out` — expect exit=0 and count 0.

proofs.line: On a file with rows 1 `{"a":1}`, 2 `{"a":`, 3 `{"b":2}`, 4 `not json`, 5 `{"c":3}`, `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 1 and its output (stdout plus stderr) contains exactly two row reports: one line starting `<file>:2:` and one line starting `<file>:4:`, and no line starting `<file>:1:`, `<file>:3:` or `<file>:5:`.
A last row with no trailing newline is still checked: on a file `{"a":1}\n{"a":` (no final newline), `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 1 and reports a line starting `<file>:2:`.
proofs.how: `printf '{"a":1}\n{"a":' > /tmp/torn.jsonl; npx --no-install jsonl-lint /tmp/torn.jsonl > /tmp/out 2>&1; echo exit=$?; grep -o '^/tmp/torn.jsonl:[0-9]*:' /tmp/out` — expect exit=1 and `/tmp/torn.jsonl:2:` only.

proofs.line: Rows ending in CRLF are judged on their content: on a file `{"a":1}\r\n{"b":2}\r\n`, `jsonl-lint <file>` exits 0.
proofs.how: `printf '{"a":1}\r\n{"b":2}\r\n' > /tmp/crlf.jsonl; npx --no-install jsonl-lint /tmp/crlf.jsonl; echo exit=$?` — expect exit=0.

proofs.line: On a path that does not exist, `jsonl-lint /nonexistent/journal.jsonl` exits 2, writes a message to stderr that contains the path `/nonexistent/journal.jsonl`, and prints no JavaScript stack trace (no line beginning with whitespace then `at `).
proofs.how: `npx --no-install jsonl-lint /nonexistent/journal.jsonl 2>/tmp/err >/tmp/out; echo exit=$?; grep -c '/nonexistent/journal.jsonl' /tmp/err; grep -cE '^\s+at ' /tmp/err /tmp/out` — expect exit=2, at least 1 match of the path on stderr, and 0 stack-trace lines.

proofs.line: Run with no file argument, `jsonl-lint` exits 2 and writes a usage message to stderr.
proofs.how: `npx --no-install jsonl-lint 2>/tmp/err; echo exit=$?; cat /tmp/err` — expect exit=2 and non-empty stderr describing usage.

proofs.line: The new workspace has a `test` script running `node:test` tests that cover a clean file, a file with invalid rows (checking the reported line numbers and exit code 1) and a missing file (exit code 2); the root `npm test` runs them and passes.
proofs.how: Run `npm ci && npm test` at the repo root: it must run the jsonl-lint workspace's tests (not print 'no workspaces under packages/') and exit 0. Read the test file(s) in the workspace to confirm they import `node:test` and cover the three cases with assertions on line numbers and exit codes; the CI `test` check on the PR must also pass.

proofs.line: The package has no runtime `dependencies` in its package.json and is plain ES modules with no build step.
proofs.how: Read packages/<tool>/package.json: no `dependencies` field (or empty), `"type": "module"` (or .mjs sources), no build script, and the bin points at a committed source file.

proofs.line: README.md's 'What is here' section no longer says there are no tools and lists jsonl-lint with how to run it.
proofs.how: Read README.md at the PR head: the 'No tools yet' bullet is gone and a bullet names jsonl-lint and shows how to invoke it on a file.

non_goals: Validating rows against a schema or checking the structure/meaning of the JSON beyond it parsing.
Repairing, rewriting or removing bad rows.
Linting several files, globs, directories or stdin in one call.
Publishing the package to npm or wiring it into the harness in suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine.
assumptions: The tool lives in a new workspace `packages/jsonl-lint` with a package.json bin named `jsonl-lint`, run as `npx --no-install jsonl-lint <file>` after `npm ci` at the root; the committed package-lock.json is updated so `npm ci` still works.
A row is one line; line numbers are 1-based and count every physical line, including blank ones.

Each invalid row is reported as one output line in the form `<file>:<line>: <reason>`, where `<file>` is the path as given; the reason text is up to the builder. Which stream (stdout or stderr) row reports go to is up to the builder.
Any JSON value (object, array, string, number, true/false/null) counts as a valid row, not only objects.
Blank or whitespace-only lines (including the empty string after a final newline) are not rows to report; a trailing `\r` from CRLF line endings is treated as whitespace.

Exit codes: 0 when every row is valid, 1 when at least one row is invalid, 2 for a usage error or a file that cannot be read (missing file included), so a caller can tell 'bad rows' from 'could not check'.
The request's 'tells me every row' means all invalid rows are reported in one run, not just the first.
